newsitem.title: UK: Britain launches review of utility regulation.
newsitem.headline: Britain launches review of utility regulation.

text.p: Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett announced Monday the launch of an interdepartmental review of the regulation of British utilities.

The review will cover the gas, electricity, water and telecommunications industries, with Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott focusing on transport. It will aim to develop general principles of regulation, Beckett told a conference.
At present each industry is regulated by an autonomous body which sets pricing and rules on other matters.
Beckett said the aim was a long-term stable framework for utility regulation which would be fair, and seen as such.
"Satisfied consumers are the key to regulatory stability," Beckett said.
The review will look at whether changes in the current regulatory framework are required. It will consider pricing formulas, but Beckett ruled out regulation on the basis of rate of return on assets.
She said the review would look at defining the limits within which regulators worked. It would examine regulation as a whole and try to identify best practices.
